13380.summary: Captive elephants arrived in trucks at Thekkinkadu Maidan in Thrissur, Kerala, for a large health camp on Friday. The Kerala Elephant Owners Federation organised the medical camp, where veterinary experts collected blood, urine, and dung samples. Federation secretary K Mahesh stated, similar medical camps would be organised in Kottayam and Kollam later this month. The samples will be analysed at Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University to introduce individual health cards and monitor medical conditions regularly.
13380.current: On October 10, 2026, captive elephants were transported in trucks to Thrissur, Kerala. The animals were brought to the location for routine health evaluations.

13560.summary: An FIR was registered for the alleged sexual abuse of a female stray dog in Bichhiaon village of Bhojpur, Bihar. Sandesh Police Station registered the case against the accused based on video evidence and a complaint from local caregiver Mukesh Kumar, following intervention by PETA India. Police filed the FIR under Section 62 read with 325 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and Sections 11(1)(a) and 11(1)(i) of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. Following a veterolegal examination by a government veterinarian, the dog is now under the care of the local caregiver.
13560.current: Following an intervention by PETA India, a police complaint was filed in Bhojpur concerning the sexual abuse of a female dog. A father of six was booked for the crime in Bihar. The complainant alleged that the accused targeted stray animals. An official case was registered regarding the incident.

13572.summary: Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary in Assam's Morigaon district has reopened for the 2026-27 tourism season, offering jeep and elephant safaris for visitors. Forest Minister Jayanta Mallabaruah formally inaugurated the season after the forest department finished repairs on internal roads. Available figures show the sanctuary hosts 106 endangered one-horned rhinoceroses. The forest department will now receive tourists for the upcoming season with thirty jeeps ready for safaris.
13572.current: Assam's Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary reopened for the 2026-27 tourism season. The announcement was made on October 13, 2026.

13718.summary: Five baby orangutans were found abandoned in an Odisha forest, raising serious concerns about illegal wildlife trafficking and exotic pet ownership in India. Nandankanan Zoo near Bhubaneswar is taking care of the animals while paperwork is under way to repatriate them to Indonesia. The author stated that worldwide wildlife smuggling is the fourth-largest criminal activity worth over USD 20 billion annually, violating rules like CITES and the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972.
13718.current: On October 14, 2026, discussions emerged regarding private zoos as a response to illegal animal smuggling. Critics note that capturing rare species harms wild populations, while escaped animals can become invasive and damage local ecosystems.

13725.summary: Declining birdlife across India is quietly eroding traditional vernacular names and cultural knowledge linked to local species, according to the State of India's Birds assessment. The 2025 update, drawing on 48 million observations from the eBird platform, evaluated 1,382 bird species and found substantial long-term declines among many groups. Researchers stated that vernacular terms like shamuk-bhanga for the Asian Openbill or Saanpmar for the Short-toed Snake-Eagle preserve vital ecological memory by connecting a species to its diet and behaviour.
13725.current: On October 12, 2026, researchers reported that shrinking bird populations in India are disrupting local ecosystems. This shift is also affecting traditional cultural knowledge and linguistic systems linked to these species.

13027.summary: A three-year-old female black panther was trapped in a cage at Kulathumon in Pathanamthitta district, marking the first time such an animal has been caught in Keralam. The forest department shifted the animal to Puthur Zoological Park, where veterinarians are monitoring its health in quarantine. Konni DFO S B Mithun Mohan stated that the panther will be released into the wild after ensuring its health condition.
13027.current: The forest department in Pathanamthitta, Kerala, captured a black panther. The animal was subsequently moved to the Puthur zoo.

13236.summary: Daniella Monet explained why she refused to dissect animals in school and shared tips on how students can help save animals. The source stated that students can learn why dissection is wrong and find easy ways to protect animals.
13236.current: An animal-welfare organization released a statement regarding Daniella Monet. The publication highlighted her opposition to biological dissection in schools.

13237.summary: A forty-year-old farmer drowned in a pond while fleeing a stray bull in Auraiya district. Police stated that Deepu Singh alias Pushpendra fell into the deep water at Purwa Bhadauriya village after a stray bull chased him while he was guarding his crops. His family found his body during a search after he failed to return home. Police sent the body for a postmortem examination and initiated an investigation.
13237.current: An agricultural worker in Auraiya attempted to get away from a stray bull. During this escape, the individual fell into the water and died by drowning.

13239.summary: Stray cattle have returned to roads and highways in Trichy as the civic body operates only one enforcement team instead of the usual two to three. Between April 1 and October 7, the Trichy corporation impounded 303 heads of cattle and collected penalties of Rs 5.3 lakh, while unclaimed bovine auctions remained pending. A senior corporation official stated that the drive will be intensified after the agency's licence lapses next month.
13239.current: Loose cattle reappeared on the streets of Trichy. This situation creates ongoing traffic hazards for local residents.

13290.summary: The Rajasthan government has sought fodder supplies from Punjab, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh to prevent a livestock feed shortage following a 17 percent rainfall deficit. Teams from the Animal Husbandry Department were deputed to visit the three neighbouring states to assess availability and supply prospects. Principal Secretary Vikas Sitaramji Bhale directed officials to monitor stocks, prevent hoarding and ensure adequate supplies in gaushalas. The department classified nine districts as critical and 22 as semi-critical, while officials assess procurement chains to secure crop residue.
13290.current: Rajasthan requested fodder shipments from Punjab, Haryana, and Madhya Pradesh. The state initiated this procurement due to looming drought conditions.

13307.summary: The Nagpur Forest Division held a specialised wildlife forensics workshop at Harisingh Sabhagruha in Seminary Hills to train forest staff in evidence handling and documentation. The Nagpur Forest Division stated that the training covered the preparation of panchanamas, primary offence reports, and forensic evidence collection to strengthen wildlife crime investigations. Officials and experts including Dr Vinita Vyas and Dr Sujit Kolangath guided participants on maintaining a clear chain of custody and legal processing.
13307.current: Forest personnel participated in an educational program. The sessions focused on the application of forensic science to wildlife matters.

13315.summary: The Gajapati Forest Division arrested six people and seized three leopard skins during raids targeting wildlife trafficking in Gajapati, Odisha. Forest officials said a special enforcement team conducted the first raid on October 8
13315.current: Law enforcement in the Gajapati district of Odisha arrested six individuals. Authorities also confiscated three leopard pelts during the operation.

13362.summary: India's first high-altitude snow leopard wildlife safari was established in Ladakh, offering guided wildlife tours along bird-watching and snow leopard trails. The initiative aims to promote tourism and conservation in the high-altitude region.
13362.current: Ladakh launched India's first high-altitude snow leopard wildlife safari. This new project establishes a specialized wildlife tourism experience in the region.

13384.summary: A rare red-headed vulture was photographed and filmed at Patal Thaur in Munsiyari, Uttarakhand, near the India-China border. Members of the Monal organisation spotted the critically endangered bird of prey while birdwatching. Wildlife expert Ranganath Pandey stated that the species faces population declines due to habitat loss and harmful veterinary drugs such as diclofenac. Continued observation will determine if the bird resides in the region or is passing through.
13384.current: A rare red-headed vulture was observed in the Uttarakhand region. The bird was spotted at an altitude of 2,650 metres in Munsiyari.

13400.summary: Joint efforts are intensified to control Classical Swine Fever affecting pigs in Car Nicobar. The Department of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services stated that an indent for 20,000 doses of vaccine has been placed for an upcoming special vaccination drive. Movement of pigs and pig products will remain restricted until the situation is controlled. Officials advised the public that the disease is not zoonotic and urged villagers to report symptoms and cooperate with monitoring teams.
13400.current: Authorities in Car Nicobar increased collaborative actions. These measures aim to manage Classical Swine Fever affecting local pigs.

13404.current: A disease concern emerged in the Gir area. The situation involves rabies affecting local lion populations as well as human residents.

13406.summary: Rabies is threatening Asiatic lions in the Greater Gir area, with two suspected deaths recorded in four months. The Gujarat govt has issued fresh directives to implement Gujarat Rabies Control Regulations, 2023, following cases in Amreli district. Experts called for stronger surveillance, testing protocols, and vaccine readiness because districts surrounding the sanctuary house at least one lakh feral dogs.
13406.current: Concerns emerged regarding the spread of rabies among the lion population. This viral disease is currently impacting the wildlife within the Gir region.

13447.summary: The Indian Army provided livestock treatment and essential medicines to help animals in Budgam, Jammu and Kashmir. The 62 Rashtriya Rifles (Dogra) Battalion organised the veterinary camp under Operation Sadbhavana, benefiting 120 local residents. The organisers stated that the programme aimed to improve animal healthcare and support villagers whose livelihoods depend on animal husbandry.
13447.current: The Indian Army provided veterinary assistance to residents in Budgam. Military personnel examined local livestock and handed out necessary medical supplies.

13454.summary: Rajasthan is set to formulate its first dedicated State Veterinary Policy to strengthen animal husbandry and improve rural livelihoods. Chief Secretary V Srinivas directed the animal husbandry department to take necessary steps for the policy, according to a senior official. Officials from the Department of Animal Husbandry stated that under the Mangla Pashu Bima Yojana, over 4.3 million animals have been registered and more than 2.6 million insurance policies issued.
13454.current: Rajasthan announced plans to create its initial state-level veterinary policy. The upcoming framework will be the first of its kind for the region.

13473.summary: A recent dog census in Shimla found 280 aggressive stray dogs among a total population of 3,070 animals in the city. The Shimla Municipal Corporation stated that the survey categorized certain animals as nervous or prone to biting people. Mayor Surinder Chauhan said the civic body will soon launch a mass sterilisation drive and expand the dog hut in the Tutikandi area to permanently house aggressive dogs.
13473.current: An animal survey took place in Shimla, Himachal Pradesh. The municipal census recorded a total of 280 aggressive dogs in the area.

13556.summary: Jadavpur University designated five on-campus areas as stray dogs feeding zones in Kolkata, requiring feeders to obtain authorisation letters from the animal welfare committee. The circular stated the measures address a rapid increase in the stray dog population exceeding 60 dogs and multiple dog bite incidents. Animal welfare committee chairman Diganta Saha stated that the procedure to determine authorised animal feeders will start after the vacation. Film studies department assistant professor Arijeet Mandal stated that the circular raises serious questions regarding legality and animal welfare.
13556.current: An educational institution established five specific locations on its grounds. These designated spots were set aside for providing meals to stray animals.

13589.summary: Sexual violence against animals in India often remains hidden due to legal gaps and the lack of a national recording system. Police in Rajkot, Gujarat arrested a man for allegedly abusing a cow, while similar incidents involving stray dogs and other animals emerged in Punjab and Rajasthan. People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) India stated it received around 50 such complaints since the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 took effect. Former police officer Rajendra Bhadu stated, "Most of the accused in these cases have been adolescent boys."
13589.current: A piece titled “Sexual violence against animals in India” was published. It addresses incidents of sexual abuse inflicted on animals within India.

13607.summary: Classical Swine Fever has affected pigs following an outbreak in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, prompting the Andaman and Nicobar Administration to launch a vaccination drive. The Department of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services began administering vaccines supplied by the Government of India on October 12, while officials also ordered strict sanitation improvements and controls on pig movement around Brookshabad. The department urged pig farmers to cooperate with veterinary officials and adopt biosecurity measures to prevent the spread of infectious diseases.
13607.current: Authorities in the Andaman islands started vaccinating pigs. This preventative measure follows an outbreak of Classical Swine Fever in the region.

13613.summary: Five baby orangutans were found abandoned in an eastern Odisha forest, sparking questions about wildlife trafficking into India. Forest officers from Balasore responded after villagers alerted patrolling teams, and the animals were later taken to Nandankanan Zoo. Pratik Prakash Indalkar stated his staff found the situation "very surprising." Lionel Hachemin of the International Fund for Animal Welfare stated it was almost certain the animals were taken from the wild due to the difficulty of obtaining five infants of the same age.
13613.current: Five infant orangutans were found left behind in India. The circumstances regarding their discovery remain unknown.

13621.summary: Four men were arrested for illegal cattle transportation involving eight cattle near Udupi in Karnataka. Kota police stated that they intercepted a pickup vehicle near Tekkatte junction on Tuesday night after receiving a tip-off. Police said the animals were being carried in a cruel manner for illegal slaughter. A case was registered under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960.
13621.current: Law enforcement arrested four individuals. These people were taken into custody for moving livestock unlawfully.

13625.summary: Simaltapu police arrested cattle smuggler Hasmat Ali during a late-night operation in Kokrajhar district, Assam, on Monday following a warning from BTC chief Hagrama Mohilary. Police said the suspect had been absconding after other members of his alleged network were caught. The Bodoland Territorial Council ordered the closure of four cattle markets to curb the illegal trade.
13625.current: Law enforcement authorities apprehended a cattle smuggler named Hasmat Ali. The arrest took place in the Kokrajhar district located in Assam.

13645.summary: The forest department seized 18 monitor lizards from a bus in Sikar district, arresting three suspects for wildlife smuggling. Assistant Conservator of Forests (Wildlife) Devendra Singh Rathore stated that the animals were packed inside two sacks during the operation near Shrimadhopur. Officials also recovered a sack of wild asparagus from the accused. Forest department officials stated that an investigation is underway to trace the source and destination of the wildlife and uncover any wider smuggling network.
13645.current: Forest officials in Sikar confiscated 18 monitor lizards. During the operation, authorities arrested three individuals for illegal wildlife trafficking.

13647.summary: Three newborn tiger cubs were born to tigress Sunaina at Tata Steel Zoological Park in Jamshedpur, with one cub recovering from an injury caused by the mother. Zoo authorities stated that the cubs arrived on September 23 and remain under continuous veterinary supervision and closed-circuit television monitoring. Tata Steel said every necessary precaution was being taken to safeguard their health and well-being. Jamshedpur residents can suggest names for the cubs via WhatsApp by October 19, and a zoo panel will select the winning entries.
13647.current: A tigress named Sunaina gave birth to her first cubs. This event took place at the JSR zoo.

13665.summary: A tiger death at Yorkshire Wildlife Park contrasts with India, where tiger encounters caused 393 deaths between 2021 and 2025. Yorkshire Wildlife Park stated that the fatality reflects how captivity, forest-based livelihoods, and human-wildlife conflict shape risks across different regions. This comparison matters because these factors govern survival and safety outcomes for both animals and people.
13665.current: A tiger died in Yorkshire. This event has caused people to question the status of hundreds of tigers in India.

13672.summary: Loud DJ music from vehicles exceeding 100 decibels distresses pets and stray dogs, causing panic and erratic behavior in Bhopal. State veterinary hospital civil surgeon Dr Smriti Desai stated, "When DJ music blasts through the streets, pets can hear high-pitched sounds that humans cannot, making the noise particularly distressing for them." Animal rights activist Swati Dixit alleged that loud sound triggers fear, injuries, and territorial fights among stray animals. The Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000, restrict nighttime loudspeakers, and authorities continue to face compliance issues regarding late-night violations.
13672.current: Loud music from DJs is reportedly causing distress to pets. This noise makes animals flee or behave in erratic ways.

13674.summary: A twenty-three-year-old man died from mob violence over suspected cattle smuggling in Raipur District, Chhattisgarh. Police stated that the victim and two others were attacked by a mob while transporting cattle on 7 June. Police appointed a Special Investigation Team to investigate the case, though no arrests were made. CSW stated, "CSW is deeply saddened by news of the passing of Saddam Qureshi and we extend our sincere condolences to his family and loved ones."
13674.current: A third Muslim man died in the hospital. He had been attacked previously over suspicions of cattle smuggling.
